title: Native memory safety: untrusted length/count sizes a copy into a fixed or freed buffer
index_line: T-0010 · MEM_WRITE · parser trusts its own length field · ASAN/KASAN oracle · corroborated
invariant_violated: The parser trusts a length/count field from the input to size or bound a memory operation on a buffer that is smaller — or already freed.

mechanism.does: attacker-crafted binary record/TLV/packet enters a length-driven parser
length/count read from the first bytes
copy/alloc walks that many bytes — bounds not re-checked against the destination on the value actually used
OOB write (overflow / undersized alloc via integer wrap) or use-after-free on a second path

source.protocol.value: protocol response/record parsers, TLV, ASN.1, packet/pcap/font chunk tables, kernel netlink/ioctls

sink.memory.copy.value: memcpy/strcpy/strcat/append into fixed dst; malloc(count*size) with attacker count

size.length.value: the untrusted length field — where it comes from and what bounds it

lifetime.object.value: UAF variant: the alloc→free→use triangle across error/teardown paths

preconditions.expr: often pre-auth — network-facing parsers are the high-value surface

success: ASAN/KASAN splat on the crafted record — decoded sanitizer report is the gold standard
deterministic crash with a controlled length field
failure_like: growable buffer + re-check against remaining space (curl socks5_recv_resp1 is the textbook safe shape)
length clamped via min() against destination size on the same value that is used
false_positive: fuzzer crash unreachable from the real input format

hazards: kernel vs userspace primitives differ (skb handling, KASAN)
allocator hardening changes exploitability, not presence — a clean crash is still a finding

provenance.author: 0security playbook corpus
provenance.corroborates: method detail + verified wins (accepted kernel UAF/stack-overflow 0-days, bluez btsnoop, bitlbee heap overflow)
